items.description: ArgoCDDeploy is a deploy repo whose chart/ pins the upstream argo-cd chart in Chart.yaml dependencies: and renders a complete Argo CD install into namespace argocd-prd, with resourceTrackingMethod: annotation (D4), controller.operation.processors: 2 (D8) and polling disabled everywhere including the ApplicationSet git generator (D6).

The AppProject `releases` (D10) exists and permits everything Argo's own Application needs to sync: argocd-prd and argocd-hooks as destinations alongside the <app>-<stage> app namespaces, a clusterResourceWhitelist covering Namespace plus every cluster-scoped kind the upstream argo-cd chart carries and migrated charts' own, and sourceRepos covering the registry repo, the deploy repos and the upstream chart repos.

Both ApplicationSets render per design.md's templates — goTemplate with missingkey=error, the glob scoped to configs/prd/, the local/upstream split on upstream.chart, the finalizer, and the templatePatch that is the conditional-autoSync mechanism — and the local-chart set passes all four hook helm parameters, hook.namespace included.
evidence: /work/AnsibleSpecs/argo-cd/design.md:201-209 — the four helm parameters; slice.md's quote of the same template omits hook.namespace
/work/Charts/charts/homelab-shared/templates/_tf-presync-hook.tpl:45-48 — all four Job arguments are `required`-guarded, so three parameters fails the render

items.description: Notifications config for Alertmanager with on-sync-failed + on-health-degraded authored (D7) — triggers, templates and a subscription that reaches every generated app, against prometheus-prd-alertmanager.prometheus-prd:9093.

SSO wiring (D9) ships in the chart: an oidc.config stanza naming issuer, client id and a client-secret reference, plus the argocd-rbac-cm line mapping the operator's identity to role:admin, with the local admin account left in place as break-glass.
The webhook secret reference is wired, and the shared secret is one value with two readers — Argo's webhook.github.secret and the relay — from one OpenBao leaf, never two.

Argo's Keycloak client exists and is recorded so keycloak-tf (Trello #68) can import rather than recreate it. Per the 2026-08-16 ruling the client is hand-created and ArgoCDDeploy ships no terraform/ and no Keycloak provider credential; the client secret reaches Argo as an ESO leaf exactly as D9 specifies.
evidence: /work/HelmCharts/_providers/providers.tf — `provider "keycloak" {}` is bare and no keycloak_* resource exists in the estate; slice 007's credential-inventory.md:48-52 records the absent leaf as deliberate

items.description: The hook namespace argocd-hooks exists with the ExternalSecret materialising argocd-hook-credentials from A.2's enumerated leaves plus the non-secret per-cluster provider configuration as template literals — one object composing a run's whole environment — the tf-presync ServiceAccount and its RBAC (PV get/list/patch), permitted as an AppProject destination (D33).
evidence: /work/AnsibleSpecs/slices/completed/007_argocd_tools_presync_hook/attachments/credential-inventory.md:32-82 — the authoritative key-by-key contract this object fills
/work/Charts/charts/homelab-shared/templates/_tf-presync-hook.tpl:27,39,51 — the Job hard-codes namespace argocd-hooks, serviceAccountName tf-presync and secret argocd-hook-credentials

items.description: Repository credential Secrets via ESO (D40), after checking whether anonymous read suffices anywhere — it suffices nowhere, so per the 2026-08-16 ruling one repo-creds Secret matching the https://github.com/pvginkel/ prefix covers the registry repo and every deploy repo, on Argo's own token rather than the hook's.

argocd-server is reachable behind the estate's exposure mechanism with homelab TLS and is-public: no — its Service carries is-public: "no" AND enable-ssl: "yes", and the vhost actually answers on 443 with a step-ca leaf, checked at the listener rather than at the annotation. And O3 is settled in favour of one fanned-out webhook endpoint: the relay at deploy-hooks.webathome.org is the only internet-facing surface, and Argo CD is not exposed to the internet.
evidence: /work/DockerImages/nginx-configurator/app/annotations.py:7-35 — exposure is nginx.webathome.org/* annotations on a Service; is-public is one flag per Service, so the relay needs its own

/work/DockerImages/nginx-configurator/app/nginxconfigurator.py:137-146,182 — certificate issuance and the RFC1918 allow block are independent switches: the step-ca leaf is the `elif entry.enable_ssl` branch, and annotations.py:145 defaults enable_ssl to False when the annotation is absent, so is-public: "no" alone yields one listen-80 server with no certificate
/work/HelmCharts/charts/kubecoder/templates/controller-service.yaml:10-13 — the estate's internal-TLS shape is both annotations together

items.description: Bootstrap happened once, by hand (operator): clone, helm dependency build, helm install; configs/prd/argocd/prd/release.yaml carries deployed: true, autoSync: false — autoSync stays false permanently for Argo itself (D3 sharp edge) — and Argo adopted itself on first generation.
evidence: kubectl get ns (2026-08-16) — no argocd* namespace exists; nothing here describes running infrastructure

items.description: The operator created the registry webhook on HelmCharts (manual, one-off) with the shared secret, pointing at the relay's public URL.
A registry push visibly regenerates (applicationset-controller receiver); a deploy-repo push visibly refreshes (argocd-server receiver).

A deliberate sync failure produces an Alertmanager notification. Read at Alertmanager's own API: its live config is the chart's stock null sink — one empty default-receiver, no route tree — so an alert lands there and goes no further, and it carries no server-name annotation either.
evidence: /work/HelmCharts/configs/prd/prometheus/prd/values.yaml:120-130 — alertmanager config sets persistence and resources only; no receivers, no route

items.description: `../config/{stage}/values.yaml` renders on the deployed Argo version (D19; fallback $values, template-only change).
$ARGOCD_APP_REVISION reaches a hook Job's args via helm parameters (D30).

items.area: R12 — the hook end to end
items.description: The hook Job runs in argocd-hooks, under the AppProject, end to end: clone → backend → apply → exit code gates the sync.
Deleting an Application whose chart carries the Prune=false Namespace does delete that namespace (D26 — if wrong, the guard changes, not the goal).

The repo-server performs helm dependency build against https://charts.home trusting the homelab CA (D17; fallback plain HTTP). Per the r1 F3 ruling the trust must reach the repo-server container itself — that pod belongs to the pinned upstream subchart, so a ConfigMap the wrapper chart renders is not evidence.
evidence: /work/Ansible/ansible/roles/baseline/files/homelab-root.crt — the source-of-truth artefact; nothing in this cluster inherits homelab CA trust, so the repo-server is wired explicitly
/work/Charts/charts/homelab-shared/Chart.yaml — homelab-shared 0.2.0 is what a consumer chart pins from https://charts.home

helm show values argo/argo-cd (chart 10.3.3 / app v3.5.1, checked 2026-08-16) — the two candidate surfaces are repoServer.volumes/volumeMounts/initContainers with the global.extraVolume* CA-bundle-over-/etc/ssl/certs example, and configs.tls.certificates, which upstream documents for repositories Argo itself resolves

items.description: Boolean deployed/autoSync behave in selector and templatePatch on the pinned version (D23), including the flag-flip generating and removing syncPolicy.automated.

items.area: R16 — the selector excludes unmigrated entries
items.description: Entries without the reconciler: key — every unmigrated release the glob matches — are excluded by the selector. missingkey=error means a leak here breaks the whole ApplicationSet, not one app.
evidence: ls /work/HelmCharts/configs/prd/*/*/release.yaml → 15 files (2026-08-16); grep -rn reconciler /work/HelmCharts/configs/ → empty. Local-chart releases carry no release.yaml at all, so the glob matches 15 entries, not the register's ~44 — the failure mode is unchanged

items.description: Point a no-sync Application at an existing live release and check the live-vs-git diff reads sensibly — diff quality proven before Phase B stakes a cutover on it.
SSO login works; local admin break-glass works (D9).

items.area: Relay proof (a) — the ruling's added item
items.description: A real GitHub delivery through the public URL lands 200 with both legs green.

items.area: Relay proof (b) — the ruling's added item
items.description: The partial-failure drill: scale one receiver to zero, redeliver, see red in GitHub's Recent Deliveries naming the dead leg, restore, redeliver green — proving that a missed delivery is always visible where it can be redelivered.
Argo runs and manages itself; the UI is reachable via Keycloak; every proof item is checked.

The throwaway app demonstrated register → deploy → undeploy → unregister with the namespace cascade (D27), and both the entry and the disposable deploy repo were deleted afterwards — the repo's .kubecoder/config.yaml entry with it.

Every repo this slice touched has a green gate: ArgoCDDeploy earns a deterministic one in its first phase — a render of the wrapper chart, not a lint of it — the disposable proof repo earns one too (chart render plus Terraform validation), and HelmCharts' existing suite stays green with the estate's first reconciler: argo-cd entry present.
evidence: /work/HelmCharts/.kubecoder/project.yaml — setup: poetry install --with test, test: pytest; no lint verb
/work/HelmCharts/tools/deploy/deploy_cli/release.py:15-28,161-171 — _RELEASE_KEYS admits the Argo keys and resolve() stops validating a non-jenkins entry as a HelmCharts release

items.description: No secret value is committed anywhere this slice touches: every credential Argo or the hook reads arrives from a named OpenBao leaf through the openbao-prd ClusterSecretStore, and the new leaves sit inside the eso AppRole's existing grant so no policy change is owed.
evidence: kubectl get clustersecretstore (2026-08-16) — openbao-prd is Valid and Ready
/work/Ansible/ansible/inventories/prd/group_vars/openbao.yml:91-96 — the eso grant's eso/prd/* glob already covers kv/eso/prd/argocd/prd/*

items.area: A.5 — the disposable proof app as build work (r1 F1 ruling)
items.description: The throwaway app is a real deploy repo, authored as a phase with its own gate and code review rather than improvised at drill time: chart/ carrying the tf-presync hook include, the Prune=false Namespace and a homelab-shared dependency from https://charts.home; a terraform/ the hook takes through clone → backend → apply against a real managed object; and config/prd/ reached as ../config/prd/values.yaml. A deliberate sync failure and a deliberate apply failure are both reachable by flipping a committed value.
evidence: /work/ArgoCDTools/presync/terraform.py:17,21-26,29-38 — a clone with no terraform/ and a clone with no config/<stage>/ are both fatal to the hook; *.tfvars are passed as -var-file in sorted order
/work/ArgoCDTools/presync/backend.py:57-72 — init supplies address/lock_address/unlock_address as -backend-config, so the repo's Terraform carries a bare backend "http" {}
/work/Charts/tests/consumer/ — Chart.yaml, values.yaml and seven templates, no terraform/ and no config/: a render fixture, not the worked example this repo has to be
